title: PS1 · Number system conversions (Ch 2)
intro: [ADDED] The original problem sets have no solutions. items.q: Perform the following number system conversions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.solution: Group 4 bits from the right: $110\;1011 \to 0110\;1011 = \mathrm{6\;B}$.
parts.method: Binary ↔ hex: groups of 4 bits, because $16 = 2^4$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.solution: Replace each octal digit by 3 bits: $1 \to 001,\ 7 \to 111,\ 4 \to 100,\ 0 \to 000,\ 0 \to 000,\ 3 \to 011$, giving $001\,111\,100\,000\,000\,011$. Drop the leading zeros.
parts.method: Octal → binary: one digit = 3 bits, because $8 = 2^3$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.solution: Group outward from the point. Whole part: $1\;0100 \to 0001\;0100 = 14$. Fraction: $1101 = \mathrm{D}$.
parts.method: Group from the radix point, padding with zeros at the outer ends.

parts.label: (d)
parts.method: Hex → binary: one digit = 4 bits.

parts.label: (e)
parts.solution: Whole part: $101\;111 = 5\;7$. Fraction: $011\;1\underline{00} = 3\;4$ (pad with zeros on the RIGHT of a fraction). Check: $57.34_8 = 47 + \frac38 + \frac4{64} = 47.4375 = 101111.0111_2$.
parts.method: Binary → octal: groups of 3 bits from the point.

parts.label: (f)
parts.method: Hex → binary digit by digit.

items.q: Convert the following numbers into decimal.

parts.label: (a)
parts.method: Radix $r$ → decimal: multiply each digit by its weight $r^i$ and add.

parts.label: (b)
parts.method: Weights are powers of 8.

parts.label: (c)
parts.solution: Whole: $16 + 4 = 20$. Fraction: $\frac12 + \frac14 + \frac1{16} = 0.8125$.
parts.method: Digits after the point have weights $2^{-1}, 2^{-2}, \ldots$

parts.label: (d)
parts.method: Weights are powers of 16; $\mathrm{A} = 10$, $\mathrm{F} = 15$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.solution: $1\cdot81 + 2\cdot27 + 0\cdot9 + 1\cdot3 + 0 = 81 + 54 + 3 = 138$. (The handout prints this as “120103”: the subscript 3 was lost.)
parts.method: Same rule for any radix, here $r = 3$.

parts.label: (f)
parts.method: Negative powers of 16 after the point.

intro: [ADDED] The original problem sets have no solutions. Compare them with your lecturer's model answers when those are released.

items.q: Prove the following equations using switching algebra.

parts.label: (a)
parts.q: $BC + D + D'(B' + C')(AD + B) = B + D$
parts.solution: First, $D'(AD + B) = AD'D + BD' = BD'$ (since $D'D = 0$). The last term becomes $BD'(B' + C') = BB'D' + BC'D' = BC'D'$. So the left side is $BC + D + BC'D'$. Now $D + D'(BC') = D + BC'$ (theorem $X + X'Y = X + Y$). Then $BC + BC' + D = B(C + C') + D = B + D$. ∎
parts.method: Expand the product, kill terms with $XX' = 0$, then combine with $X + X'Y = X + Y$ and $XY + XY' = X$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.solution: By DeMorgan, $(B' + C') = (BC)'$. By consensus, $AB + A'C = AB + A'C + BC$, so the left side is $AB + A'C + BC + (BC)'D$. Since $X + X'D = X + D$ with $X = BC$: $= AB + A'C + BC + D$. Remove the consensus term $BC$ again: $= AB + A'C + D$. ∎
parts.method: Add a consensus term to create an $X + X'Y$ pattern, then remove it again.

items.q: Use switching-algebra theorems to simplify each function.

parts.label: (a)
parts.solution: Covering ($X + XY = X$): $A + ABC + AB'C' = A$. What's left is $A + BC + B'C'$, and $BC + B'C'$ is the XNOR of $B$ and $C$.
parts.method: Covering removes every term that already contains $A$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.solution: $AB + AB' = A$ and $A'B + A'B' = A'$, so the inside is $A + A' = 1$ and $F = 1' = 0$. (The four terms are all four minterms of $A, B$.)
parts.method: Combining theorem $XY + XY' = X$, then $X + X' = 1$.

items.q: Write the canonical sum from the shorthand.

parts.method: Write each row number in binary; complement the variables that are 0.

parts.solution: $1 = 001 \to A'B'C$, $2 = 010 \to A'BC'$, $4 = 100 \to AB'C'$, $6 = 110 \to ABC'$. (Not asked, but it simplifies to $A'B'C + BC' + AC'$.)
parts.method: Canonical sum = OR of the minterms, each containing every variable.

items.q: Use Karnaugh maps to find a minimal sum of products.

parts.label: (a)
parts.solution: Cells 1, 3, 5, 7 all have $z = 1$: one group of 4 → $z$. Cell 6 (110) pairs with 7 (111) → $xy$. Two groups cover every 1.
parts.method: Make each group as large as possible (a power of 2), and use as few groups as possible.

parts.label: (b)
parts.solution: 4, 5, 6, 7 (row $w'x$) → $w'x$. 6, 7, 14, 15 (column $xy$) → $xy$. 1 (0001) and 9 (1001) differ only in $w$ → $x'y'z$. The exact minimizer confirms this is the only minimal sum (3 terms, 7 literals).
parts.method: Look for the groups of 4 first; then cover the leftovers with the largest group that contains them.

items.q: Use Karnaugh maps to find a minimal sum of products; d(…) are don't-cares.

parts.label: (a)
parts.solution: $0, 1, 8, 9_d \to x'y'$ (group of 4 using $d$9). $0, 1, 2, 3_d \to w'x'$. $1, 3_d, 9_d, 11 \to x'z$ (the only way to put 11 in a group of 4). $d$15 is not needed.
parts.method: Use a don't-care only when it makes a group bigger; never cover a group of only d's.

parts.label: (b)
parts.method: Don't-cares let two groups of 4 replace smaller ones.

intro: [ADDED] The original problem sets have no solutions. items.q: Simplify and implement with a PLD; draw the circuit in compact representation. $F_1 = A'BCD + AC'D' + B'CD$, $F_2 = A'B + AB' + C'D + CD'$, $F_3 = (A + B + CD)(A' + B + C' + D) + A'B'C'$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.solution: Minterms: $A'BCD = 7$, $AC'D' = 8, 12$, $B'CD = 3, 11$, so $F_1 = \Sigma(3, 7, 8, 11, 12)$. On the K-map, 3 and 7 pair → $A'CD$; 3 and 11 pair → $B'CD$; 8 and 12 pair → $AC'D'$. (Algebraically: $A'BCD + B'CD = CD(A'B + B') = CD(A' + B')$, which expands to $A'CD + B'CD$.)
parts.method: K-map on the minterm list; 15 is not in $F_1$, so $CD$ alone can't be used.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: $F_2 = A'B + AB' + C'D + CD'$  $(= A \oplus B + C \oplus D)$
parts.solution: It is already minimal: each pair is an XOR, and the K-map (12 ones, zeros only at 0, 3, 12, 15) has no group of 4 or 8, so it needs four groups of 2.
parts.method: Check minimality with the K-map before 'simplifying' further.

parts.label: (c)
parts.solution: Use $(X + B)(Y + B) = B + XY$ with $X = A + CD$, $Y = A' + C' + D$: $XY = AC' + AD + A'CD + CD = AC' + AD + CD$. So $F_3 = B + AC' + AD + CD + A'B'C'$. Since $B + B'(A'C') = B + A'C'$: $F_3 = B + AC' + A'C' + AD + CD = B + C' + AD + CD$. Then $C' + CD = C' + D$, and $D$ covers $AD$: $F_3 = B + C' + D$. Check: $F_3 = 0$ only for $B = 0, C = 1, D = 0$ (minterms 2 and 10).
parts.method: Factor the common $B$ out of the product of sums first, then use $X + X'Y = X + Y$ twice.

parts.label: (d)
parts.q: Draw the PLA in compact representation.
parts.solution: Each row of the AND array is one product term; a dot means 'this literal is connected'. Each column of the OR array is one output; a dot means 'this term is ORed in'. $F_1$ uses $A'CD, B'CD, AC'D'$; $F_2$ uses $A'B, AB', C'D, CD'$; $F_3$ uses the one-literal terms $B, C', D$. No term is shared here, so a PAL would work just as well.
parts.method: Compact (dot) notation from Ch 6: draw only the connections you keep.

items.q: Implement each function using a 4-to-16 decoder (active-low outputs, like the 74x154) and NAND gates.

parts.solution: Inputs $A, B, C, D$ drive the decoder's select inputs ($A$ = MSB). Each active-low output $\overline{Y_i}$ is 0 exactly for minterm $i$. $F = Y_0 + Y_4 + \cdots + Y_{14} = (\overline{Y_0}\cdot\overline{Y_4}\cdots\overline{Y_{14}})'$ by DeMorgan, which is a NAND of those outputs.
parts.method: Decoder = minterm generator; OR of active-low lines = NAND.

parts.solution: First expand to a canonical sum: $A'BCD = 7$; $AC'D' \to 8, 12$; $B'CD \to 3, 11$. Then NAND the matching decoder outputs, exactly as in (1).
parts.method: Always convert to minterms first; the decoder can't use a simplified form.
